- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The ideal temperature for planting tomatoes outside is when the soil temperature reaches around 55°F (13°C) to 60°F (16°C) and the air temperature is around 65°F (18°C) to 70°F (21°C).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For marigolds, the ideal soil temperature for planting outside is around 50°F (10°C) to 55°F (13°C).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should check the average last frost date for their area online before planting.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should harden off seedlings by gradually exposing them to outdoor conditions over 7-10 days.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should check specific instructions for each type of seedling or plant they are growing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To transplant seedlings without shocking them, user should prepare new pots, water seedlings, gather materials, handle roots with care, inspect and trim roots, add fresh potting soil, place seedlings, firm the soil, water thoroughly, and monitor after transplanting.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should transplant in the morning or late afternoon to avoid direct sunlight and avoid transplanting during extreme weather conditions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User's mix of peat moss, vermiculite, and perlite is suitable for seedlings, including marigolds.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User might consider adding compost to their mix for nutrients and adjusting the ratio of peat moss, vermiculite, and perlite for better drainage and aeration.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A suggested adjusted mix could be 20-30% peat moss, 30-40% vermiculite, 30-40% perlite, and 10-20% compost.
